scores.evidence: There are four can-do objectives (o1 apply 「書き換えて使える」, o2 analyze 「見分け…聞き出せる」, o3 evaluate 「判断できる」, o4 create 「作って直せる」). Each has two or more graded items: o1 q1/q5, o2 q2/q6, o3 q3/q7, o4 q4/q8/q10/q9. o1 and o3 each have an apply- or transfer-level item set in a new context (q5 料理教室, q7 水やり記録).

hook-b1 sets up the problem in three concrete sentences: 「家計簿アプリを作って」, then 「グラフや分類が並んだ画面」, then 「どこから直せばよいのか、分からなくなってしまいました」. The ungraded predict q0 asks what was missing and has feedback on every distractor. There is no trivia or statistics.

The prerequisites list ch0 and ch1. s1-b1 recalls ch0 (「ビジョンを示すこと」), ex-data recalls the ch1 database, and PRD and 仕様書 are glossed. However, 目的 is the deciding idea in q0's explanation and in q1's correct option d 「目的が決まるまで…」, but it is only defined later in s2-defs (2-2).

Each segment covers one idea, introduces at most 2 new terms, and has a table, definitions or quiz on every screen, and lint is clean. The lesson-level budgets are still exceeded: estMinutes is 30 (the contract allows 8–20), body text is about 3,050 JP characters (budget 2,400), and the explanation text in 2-5 is about 460 characters including the table (segment budget 300).

s3-steps is a complete 6-step worked example on 家計簿. Each step has a subgoal title and a reason (e.g. ex-data 「決めないと、項目をAIが推測で選ぶことになります」) and comes before the practice. There is no faded example in between: the practice jumps straight to the learner's own topic.

All four content segments end with an inline check in a new context (q1 犬の散歩, q2 送迎当番, q3 読書記録), and every wrong option has feedback. Two answers can be spotted from surface cues: in q1 and q4 the correct option is the shortest, and q1 d echoes the lesson's key word 「目的」 against the feature-focused option b.

All four misconceptions in the brief are corrected in the body with reasons. AI as mind-reader: s1-b5. Plan must be perfect: s3-b1 「最初から完璧でなくてかまいません」. Include every feature: s5-b1. Goal vs feature: s2-table. Distractors encode real beliefs (q4 a 「AIが意図を読み取り…」, q8 b 「念のためMustに」), and each feedback corrects them in 2 sentences or fewer.

There is one diagram (s2-b4) with 3 nodes, and it shows a process: the screen flow. Its labels match ex-screens (「今月の残り画面」「支出の入力画面」), its caption states the takeaway 「Mustだけなら、最初の版の画面は2つで足りる」, and it has alt text. There are no images.

The practice is an authentic transfer task (the learner's own app, with a club-app fallback). It has 6 steps, each with expect and hint, troubleshoot on ②④⑥, a model answer in practice-prompt.expect and a 6-item checklist. However, steps ② and ⑤ point back to prompts in 2-1 and 2-4 (「2-1の「壁打ちを始める依頼文」」), so the learner has to scroll up two sections in the middle of the task. The model answer also does not show a revision for ⑥.

The summary (4 points) comes after the exam. summary-next has a reflection question (「Won'tに入れる機能は何でしょう？理由も1つ」) and the next step (ch3 VS Code, ch4 hand over the plan). There are 6 flashcards and askTutor suggestions.

I re-fetched the cc-best-practices source and its quotes match: "can't read your mind", "solves the wrong problem", "interview you" and "state what is out of scope". The MVP definition (s5-defs) follows Ries, and the MoSCoW meanings (s5-b2) follow the Agile Business Consortium. The prompts are tool-agnostic (target any). The reader label 「期待される結果」 cited in practice-tip exists in PromptBlock.tsx.
The text uses consistent です・ます, is warm (「完璧でなくてかまいません」), has no banned phrases, and uses terms consistently (通知, やらないこと). One clunky spot remains: the q4 explanation stacks こと: 「範囲外のことを書くことを挙げています」.

Every learner-facing string has both jp and en, including the diagram labels and alt text, and there are no links or baked-in text. The EN q1 explanation is hard to parse: "whose problem you want to solve, and what it is, turn into words".

niceToHave: load / lesson: estMinutes 30 and about 3,050 JP characters of body text are above the contract's 8–20 minutes and 2,400 characters. The owner should consider splitting the practice into its own lesson, or the author could trim s3-intro and the 2-5 lead to bring the 2-5 segment closer to 300 characters.

prior / s1-check q1: the correct option depends on 目的 vs 機能, which is taught only in 2-2. Either add one sentence in s1-b5 (e.g. 「機能より先に、誰の何のためかを聞いてもらいます」) or move the goal-vs-feature contrast out of q1.
active / q1, q4: lengthen the correct option slightly (q1 d, q4 d) so it is not the shortest option.

practice / practice-steps: put compact copies of the 2-1 and 2-4 prompts (or in-page anchors) next to steps ② and ⑤ so the learner does not have to scroll back two sections. Also add a one-line sample revision for ⑥ to the model answer.
worked / s3-steps→practice: one faded step (e.g. ex-moscow with Should/Could/Won't left for the learner to fill) would raise this to 4.
voice / s3-check explanation: 「範囲外のことを書くことを挙げています」 → 「範囲外を明記することを挙げています」 or similar.
a11y_l10n / s1-check explanation (en): rewrite as "Questions about the goal, not the features, help you put into words whose problem you're solving."
summary: The biggest strength is alignment: every objective has inline and exam items in new contexts, and every misconception in the brief is corrected both in the body and in the distractor feedback, with sources I checked against the live page. Every criterion scores 3 or more, the mean is 3.46, and there are no must-fix items. The most important remaining fix is length: 30 minutes and about 3,050 JP characters are over the contract budget, and the practice sends learners back to prompts in 2-1 and 2-4.
